heroData.title: EOR & PEO in Greece
heroData.subtitle: Hire in Athens and Thessaloniki Without a Local Entity
heroData.description: Our Greece Employer of Record (EOR) solution allows you to onboard talent in days. We handle monthly EFKA contributions, ERGANI filings, and the mandatory 13th/14th month salary payments while you manage the day-to-day work.
heroData.bestFor: Market Entry, Remote Tech Teams, Sales Reps

steps.title: Contract Drafting
steps.description: Preparation of a compliant Greek employment contract. While under Greek law a written statement of terms is required within 2 months, our EOR provides a full contract upfront covering hours, compensation, and 14-salary structure.

steps.title: EFKA Registration
steps.description: Registration of the employee with the Unified Social Security Fund (e-EFKA) on their first day. Employees must obtain a Social Security Fund Number (AMA) within 15 days.

steps.title: ERGANI Submission
steps.description: Mandatory digital submission of the hiring announcement (E3 form) to the ERGANI Information Sub-system before work commences.

steps.title: Digital Work Card Setup
steps.description: Integration with the 'Digital Work Card' (Ψηφιακή Κάρτα Εργασίας) via the myErgani app for real-time tracking of arrival and departure times.

steps.title: Induction & Equipment
steps.description: Finalizing local benefit enrollment and ensuring payroll data (bank account, tax ID/AFM) is correctly mapped for the first month's payment.

rows.label: Employer Social Security (EFKA)
values: Includes health, pension, and unemployment. Monthly cap applies.

rows.label: EOR Management Fee
values: Flat fee per employee; varies by volume and complexity.

rows.label: Annual Admin Fee
values: Mandatory annual per-employee social security fee.

rows.label: Setup Fee
values: One-time fee for registration and contract setup.

items.title: Digital Work Card Penalties
items.text: Incorrect use or failure to scan the Digital Work Card can result in fines of up to €10,500 per violation for the employer. Real-time logging is strictly enforced.

items.title: Probation Periods
items.text: Statutory probation is typically 12 months, during which termination can occur without severance. However, collective agreements may shorten this period.

items.title: Notice Periods
items.text: After the first year, notice periods range from 1 to 4 months depending on seniority. Severance pay is mandatory for terminations with notice (half of the full severance if notice is given).

items.title: Christmas Bonus
items.text: Equivalent to 1 full month's salary, paid in December.

items.title: Easter Bonus
items.text: Equivalent to 0.5 month's salary, paid before Orthodox Easter.

items.title: Summer Bonus
items.text: Equivalent to 0.5 month's salary, paid when the employee takes annual leave (usually July/August).

faqs.question: Can I hire non-EU citizens through a Greece EOR?
faqs.answer: Yes, but the EOR must sponsor a work permit. This is common for high-skilled tech roles, but requires a longer lead time (3-6 months) for visa processing.

faqs.question: Is insurance provided by the EOR?
faqs.answer: The EOR manages the statutory EFKA health insurance. Many international companies choose to add private supplementary health insurance as a perk.

faqs.question: What is the maximum working hours?
faqs.answer: Standard is 40 hours per week. Overtime is regulated and must be recorded on the Digital Work Card.

steps.title: Attendance Synchronization
steps.description: Extract data from the ERGANI Digital Work Card to verify hours worked, overtime, and leave.

steps.title: Bonus Calculation
steps.description: Pro-rating Easter, Summer, or Christmas bonuses depending on the specific month and employee tenure.

steps.title: Net-to-Gross Processing
steps.description: Applying EFKA deductions (13.87% employee) and progressive income tax withholdings.

steps.title: Statutory Remittance
steps.description: Payment of EFKA contributions by the end of the following month and filing of the APD (Analytical Periodic Statement).

steps.title: Disbursement
steps.description: Transfer of net salary to local Greek IBANs by the end of the calendar month.

items.title: Solidarity Tax Abolishment
items.text: Note that the special solidarity contribution tax was fully abolished for private sector employees as of Jan 1, 2023.

items.title: Family Allowances
items.text: Payroll must account for child allowances and marital status, which can impact the net-take-home pay through tax credits.

items.title: Payment Penalties
items.text: Late payment of EFKA contributions triggers automatic interest and surcharges. Accuracy in the APD statement is critical to avoid audits.

faqs.question: Are 14 salaries mandatory in the private sector?
faqs.answer: Yes, the 13th and 14th salaries (distributed as Christmas, Easter, and Summer bonuses) are legally mandatory for all private sector employees in Greece.

faqs.question: Can I pay employees in USD/GBP?
faqs.answer: Payroll must be calculated in EUR for statutory reporting. While the net contract can mention other currencies, the actual disbursement and tax calculation must follow EUR standards.

faqs.question: What is the payroll deadline?
faqs.answer: Most companies process payroll between the 20th and 25th to ensure payment by the last working day of the month.

steps.title: Determine Annual Gross
steps.description: In Greece, remember to multiply the monthly gross by 14 to get the true annual gross salary.

steps.title: Duct Social Security
steps.description: Apply the ~13.87% EFKA employee deduction from the monthly gross.

steps.title: Apply Income Tax
steps.description: Calculate tax based on progressive brackets (9%, 22%, 28%, 36%, 44%) on the remaining taxable amount.

steps.title: Add Employer Costs
steps.description: Add ~22.29% for employee social insurance to find the Total Cost of Employment.

steps.title: Factor in Bonuses
steps.description: Ensure the Easter (0.5), Vacation (0.5), and Christmas (1.0) bonuses are accrued for in the annual total.

items.title: The 14-Salary Multiplier
items.text: Greece mandates 14 salaries per year. These bonuses are paid based on specific dates: Easter in April, Vacation in July, and Christmas in December.

items.title: Salary Minima
items.text: As of Jan 2025, the minimum monthly gross salary for unskilled workers is being reviewed (expected around €830+). Never calculate below legal thresholds.

items.title: Family Discounts
items.text: Individual income tax is reduced via tax credits based on the number of dependent children.

faqs.question: Is there a Solidarity Contribution?
faqs.answer: For private sector employees, the Special Solidarity Contribution has been permanently abolished as of 2023.

faqs.question: Does the calculator include meal vouchers?
faqs.answer: Non-taxable benefits like meal vouchers (up to €6/day) are typically added after net pay calculation.

faqs.question: Are the rates different for part-time?
faqs.answer: The percentages remain the same, but the total tax burden may be lower due to the lower tax brackets.

heroData.title: Incorporation in Greece
heroData.subtitle: Set Up Your Business in the Hellenic Republic
heroData.description: Establish your legal presence in Greece quickly. From the flexible IKE (Private Capital Company) to the traditional AE (Société Anonyme), we guide you through GEMI registration and tax activation.

steps.title: Name Reservation
steps.description: Submission of the desired company name to the General Commercial Registry (GEMI) for availability check and reservation.

steps.title: Articles of Association
steps.description: Drafting of the statute using the 'One-Stop Service' model statute (to bypass notary requirements) or customized articles.

steps.title: Digital Submission
steps.description: Filing via the Electronic One-Stop Service (e-YMS). Registration is typically completed within 24-72 hours.

steps.title: Tax ID (AFM) Issuance
steps.description: Automatic issuance of the company Tax Identification Number upon successful GEMI registration.

steps.title: Final Activation
steps.description: Registration with the EFKA (Social Security) and setup of the local business bank account.

items.title: The IKE Flexibility
items.text: The IKE is the most popular corporate form in Greece due to its €1 capital requirement and the ability to contribute 'capital', 'extra-capital' (e.g. labor), or 'guarantee' contributions.

items.title: UBO Registry
items.text: All Greek companies must register their Ultimate Beneficial Owners (UBO) in the Central Registry within 60 days of incorporation.

items.title: Golden Visa Context
items.text: Business investment in Greece can sometimes be leveraged for residency permits (Golden Visa), though rules for real estate vs. business differ significantly.

rows.label: Legal & Drafting Fees
values: Varies by complexity of the AoA.

faqs.question: Can a foreigner be a manager?
faqs.answer: Yes, EU and non-EU citizens can manage Greek companies. Non-EU residents may need a specific residence permit for business activity.

faqs.question: Is a physical office mandatory?
faqs.answer: Yes, a Greek company must have a physical registered address (headquarters) for tax purposes.

faqs.question: How long does it take?
faqs.answer: With the e-YMS system, an IKE can be incorporated digitally in as little as 3 business days.

heroData.title: Staffing in Greece
heroData.subtitle: Discover Top Talent in the Mediterranean Hub
heroData.description: Access Greece's highly educated workforce. We specialize in sourcing tech, maritime, and seasonal hospitality talent while ensuring all recruitment practices meet EU transparency standards.
heroData.bestFor: Rapid Recruitment, Tech Hiring, Remote Expansion

steps.title: Market Benchmarking
steps.description: Analyzing local salary expectations (including the 14-salary norm) to ensure a competitive offer.

steps.title: Multi-Channel Sourcing
steps.description: Leveraging LinkedIn, local job boards (Karyera, Skywalker), and university networks.

steps.title: Compliance Screening
steps.description: Verifying right-to-work status for non-EU candidates and checking academic credentials.

steps.title: Technical Assessment
steps.description: Coordinating interviews and skill tests tailored to the specific role requirements.

steps.title: Offer Management
steps.description: Managing salary negotiations and contract signing ensures a smooth handoff to the EOR or internal HR.

items.title: The Tech Talent Boom
items.text: Greece (especially Athens) is emerging as a tech hub. Skilled software engineers are plentiful but increasingly transition to remote global roles.

items.title: Salary Transparency
items.text: EU Pay Transparency Directive rules apply: be prepared to disclose salary ranges in job postings or before the first interview.

items.title: Language Proficiency
items.text: Greek professionals typically have high English proficiency, especially in Athens, making it an ideal location for international support hubs.

items.title: GDPR Compliance
items.text: Strict adherence to data protection for candidate resumes and personal information is mandatory under Greek and EU law.

items.title: Anti-Discrimination
items.text: Greek labor law prohibits discrimination on the basis of gender, age, race, or religion in the hiring process.

items.title: Work Permits
items.text: Hiring non-EU nationals requires a specific work visa (Type D) and local residence permit approval.

faqs.question: What is the notice period for new hires?
faqs.answer: Contract notice periods depend on length of service. During the first year of employment, the statutory notice period is zero (probation).

faqs.question: Are background checks standard?
faqs.answer: Yes, criminal record checks and degree verification are standard for executive and finance roles.

faqs.question: Can I use contractors for seasonal work?
faqs.answer: Yes, but be careful of misclassification. Repeated short-term contracts may be deemed permanent by the Labour Inspectorate (SEPE).

heroData.title: HRIS in Greece
heroData.subtitle: Digital Workforce Management with Ergani Integration
heroData.description: Modernize your HR with systems that natively support the Greece Digital Work Card and real-time ERGANI II reporting. Manage 14-salary payroll, leave tracking, and document storage in a single platform.

steps.title: Data Migration
steps.description: Existing employee records (AFM, AMKA, Salary history) are migrated from legacy systems or spreadsheets.

steps.title: Ergani API Mapping
steps.description: Connecting the HRIS to the ERGANI II web service using the company's business credentials.

steps.title: Rule Configuration
steps.description: Setting up local rules for leave (20-25 days), public holidays, and overtime calculation policies.

steps.title: Work Card Pilot
steps.description: Testing the QR code capture and real-time reporting for a small subset of employees before full rollout.

steps.title: Manager Training
steps.description: Training local managers on how to approve leave and handle 'Work Card' anomalies within the platform.

items.title: The End of Paper Files
items.text: As of Jan 2025, Greece is phasing out physical leave books. A compliant HRIS that stores this digitally is now the legal gold standard.

items.title: Work Card Anomalies
items.text: The ERGANI system flags delays. Your HRIS should provide real-time alerts if an employee forgets to clock out to avoid fines.

items.title: ESS (Employee Self-Service)
items.text: Greek employees highly value mobile access. Mobile-first HRIS options see much higher engagement for expense and leave requests.

items.title: Overtime Declaration
items.text: System must track and report overtime via the E8 form in ERGANI before it is performed.

items.title: Leave Declaration
items.text: Annual leave must be declared in ERGANI (E11 form) within the first month of the following year.

items.title: Annual Personnel Table
items.text: All employers must submit an annual personnel table (E4 form) detailing staff, hours, and salaries.

faqs.question: Does the system support Greek language?
faqs.answer: Yes, for local compliance and employee adoption, we recommend systems with a full Greek localization.

faqs.question: Is cloud hosting safe for Greek data?
faqs.answer: Provided the server is within the EU (GDPR), cloud hosting is safe and widely used by Greek enterprises.

faqs.question: Can I track field staff with a work card?
faqs.answer: Yes, the myErgani app is designed for mobile clocking, making it ideal for staff working at various locations.

heroData.title: Accounting Services in Greece
heroData.subtitle: Compliant Financial Management with MyDATA Integration
heroData.description: Navigate the complexities of Geek GAAP and the mandatory MyDATA digital platform. From monthly bookkeeping to annual financial statements, we ensure your accounts are transparent and audit-ready.

steps.title: Invoicing via MyDATA
steps.description: Issuance of electronic invoices and real-time transmission to the Independent Authority for Public Revenue (AADE).

steps.title: Expense Tracking
steps.description: Collection and categorization of business expenses, ensuring and matching with MyDATA electronic records.

steps.title: Bank Reconciliation
steps.description: Matching bank statements with accounting entries to ensure cash flow accuracy.

steps.title: VAT Return Submission
steps.description: Preparation and filing of the monthly (for double-entry) or quarterly (for single-entry) VAT return.

steps.title: Management Reporting
steps.description: Generation of P&L and Balance Sheet reports for internal stakeholders and global consolidation if required.

items.title: MyDATA Mandatory Reporting
items.text: As of 2024, nearly all Greek businesses must use the MyDATA platform for e-invoicing. Manual books are largely obsolete.

items.title: Late Filing Fines
items.text: Fines for late VAT or income tax submissions can be significant, starting from €100 for simple delays and scaling with tax due.

items.title: Digital Invoicing Speed
items.text: Using an integrated accounting-invoicing software can reduce manual entry time by up to 60% and eliminate MyDATA sync errors.

items.title: Single-Entry (B' Class)
items.text: Used by small businesses and individual entrepreneurs with turnover under €1.5M.

items.title: Double-Entry (G' Class)
items.text: Mandatory for AE, EPE, and IKE companies. Requires a more rigorous bookkeeping standard.

items.title: IFRS Option
items.text: Large companies or those part of international groups may opt to follow International Financial Reporting Standards.

faqs.question: What is the fiscal year in Greece?
faqs.answer: The fiscal year follows the calendar year (January 1 to December 31).

faqs.question: Can I keep my books in English?
faqs.answer: The statutory books must be in Greek, but management reports and internal documents can be in English.

faqs.question: Is an external audit mandatory?
faqs.answer: Mandatory for large companies (AE) exceeding certain asset and turnover thresholds. For others, it is optional but recommended for transparency.

steps.title: Risk Assessment
steps.description: Conducting a mandatory written risk assessment for the workplace provided by a qualified Safety Officer.

steps.title: GDPR Mapping
steps.description: Identifying data flows, appointing a DPO (if required), and updating privacy policies and employee contracts.

steps.title: Labour Law Audit
steps.description: Reviewing employment contracts to ensure compliance with the latest 'Ergani II' and Work Card requirements.

steps.title: Internal Policies
steps.description: Implementing Whistleblowing channels (mandatory for 50+ staff) and Anti-Harassment policies.

steps.title: Ongoing Monitoring
steps.description: Regular quarterly reviews to adapt to changes in Greek and EU regulations.

items.title: Whistleblowing Hotline
items.text: Law 4990/2022 makes reporting channels mandatory for all companies with 50+ employees. Non-compliance leads to heavy fines.

items.title: Labour Inspectorate (SEPE)
items.text: SEPE audits are frequent. Ensure all Work Card logs and overtime forms are updated in real-time.

items.title: Safety Officer Hours
items.text: The hours a Safety Officer must spend on-site depend on the 'Risk Category' and number of employees. Most offices fall into Category C (Low Risk).

items.title: AADE
items.text: The Independent Authority for Public Revenue - governs all tax and customs matters.

items.title: HDPA
items.text: Hellenic Data Protection Authority - enforces GDPR and privacy laws.

items.title: SEPE
items.text: The Labour Inspectorate - monitors employment law and workplace safety compliance.

faqs.question: What is a 'Technikos Asfaleias'?
faqs.answer: A Safety Officer (Legal requirement) who oversees workplace safety, provides staff training, and registers risks.

faqs.question: Is insurance mandatory for employees?
faqs.answer: State health insurance (EFKA) is mandatory. Private health or life insurance is a highly valued benefit but not legally required.

faqs.question: What are the rules for remote work contracts?
faqs.answer: Since 2021, Law 4808/2021 defines rules for remote work, including the 'Right to Disconnect' and equipment cost reimbursement.

steps.title: Corporate Tax Return
steps.description: Submission of the annual corporate tax return (Form N) by the sixth month after the end of the fiscal year.

steps.title: Withholding Tax Filing
steps.description: Monthly filing and payment of withholding taxes on salaries, royalties, and professional fees.

steps.title: VIES/Intrastat
steps.description: Reporting of intra-community acquisitions and supplies of goods/services to the EU.

steps.title: Local Property Tax (ENFIA)
steps.description: Annual filing and management of property-related taxes for companies owning real estate in Greece.

steps.title: Transfer Pricing
steps.description: Preparation of local and master files for transactions with related parties (if thresholds met).

items.title: R&D Incentives
items.text: Greece offers significant tax breaks for R&D spending, including an extra 100% deduction on qualified expenses.

items.title: Advance Tax Payment
items.text: New companies must pay a portion (often 50-80%) of next year's estimated tax in advance, though discounts for first years exist.

items.title: Double Tax Treaties
items.text: Greece has a vast network of DTAs. Ensure you have 'Tax Residency Certificates' for cross-border payments to apply lower rates.

items.title: Flat Tax for New Residents
items.text: High-net-worth individuals moving to Greece may opt for a €100k flat tax on global income for 15 years.

items.title: Digital Nomad Tax Break
items.text: Qualifying remote workers can get a 50% income tax exemption for the first 7 years of residency.

items.title: Social Security Cap
items.text: Employee and employer social security contributions are capped at a monthly gross salary of €7,373.

faqs.question: What is the statute of limitations for tax audits?
faqs.answer: Typically 5 years, but it can be extended in cases of tax evasion or new data.

faqs.question: Are digital assets taxed?
faqs.answer: Yes, capital gains from crypto-assets are generally taxed as capital gains income (15%), though specific guidance is evolving.

faqs.question: Does Greece have a carbon tax?
faqs.answer: Greece follows EU ETS regulations and has specific environmental taxes on fuels and plastic containers.

heroData.title: Managed Services Agreement
heroData.subtitle: Outcome-Based Professional Services
heroData.description: Engage under results-driven agreements for IT, BPO, or facilities management. We ensure your Greek MSAs are legally sound, with clear KPIs and intellectual property protections for multi-year partnerships.
heroData.bestFor: Project Outsourcing, IT Support, Back-office Hubs

steps.title: SOW Definition
steps.description: Drafting a detailed Statement of Work with clear deliverables, timelines, and acceptance criteria.

steps.title: Service Level Agreement (SLA)
steps.description: Defining uptime, response times, and quality benchmarks with associated penalties for non-performance.

steps.title: IP Rights Clause
steps.description: Ensuring that all intellectual property created during the service is transferred to the client under Greek Law.

steps.title: Liability & Indemnity
steps.description: Setting caps on liability and defining insurance requirements for the service provider.

steps.title: Governance Setup
steps.description: Establishing monthly review meetings and escalation paths for project management.

items.title: Outsourcing vs. Staffing
items.text: Greek law distinguishes between 'Service Provision' (MSA) and 'Temporary Staffing'. MSAs must focus on outcomes, not constant supervision of individuals.

items.title: Exit Strategy
items.text: Ensure your MSA includes clear 'Termination for Convenience' clauses and data handover procedures to avoid vendor lock-in.

items.title: Local Law Choice
items.text: For services performed in Greece, local labour and data laws are often mandatory even if the contract is under foreign governing law.

items.title: Subcontracting Approval
items.text: Contracts should clearly state if the provider is allowed to use subcontractors and who bears the liability.

items.title: Data Processing Annex
items.text: A DPA is essential for any MSA where the provider has access to personal data of employees or customers.

items.title: Confidentiality & NDAs
items.text: Robust non-disclosure clauses are standard to protect proprietary trade secrets during service delivery.

faqs.question: Is VAT applicable to MSAs?
faqs.answer: Yes, 24% VAT is standard. For cross-border services, the 'Reverse Charge' mechanism may apply within the EU.

faqs.question: Can I white-label the services?
faqs.answer: Yes, MSAs can be structured for white-labeled deliverables, provided IP rights are assigned.

faqs.question: What is the typical duration?
faqs.answer: MSAs usually range from 1 to 3 years with annual performance reviews.

steps.title: Requirements Audit
steps.description: Defining your business needs, specifically focusing on Greek statutory integrations (MyDATA, Ergani).

steps.title: Vendor Selection
steps.description: Evaluating local vs. global vendors based on localization, UI support, and regulatory compliance.

steps.title: System Configuration
steps.description: Customizing the software for local tax codes, VAT rates, and employee benefit rules.

steps.title: Integration Testing
steps.description: Verifying the seamless flow of data between your HRIS, Payroll, and Accounting modules.

steps.title: Rollout & Training
steps.description: Onboarding your Greek team and providing training on the new digital workflows.

items.title: Cloud-First Mandatory
items.text: With the rise of remote work and real-time state reporting, cloud-based software is now essential for 2025 operations in Greece.

items.title: API Reliability
items.text: Ensure your software uses reliable APIs for Ergani/MyDATA. Delays in system-to-state reporting can trigger compliance flags.

items.title: Voucher Programs
items.text: The Greek government frequently offers 'Digital Transformation' vouchers to cover up to 90% of software costs for SMEs.

items.title: AI in Greek HR
items.text: Growing adoption of AI-driven recruitment and sentiment analysis within local Athenian enterprises.

items.title: Cybersecurity Focus
items.text: Increased investment in EU-based data hosting and security as Greek businesses prepare for NIS2 compliance.

items.title: Low-Code/No-Code
items.text: Growing use of rapid application development platforms within Greek startups to accelerate digital transformation.

faqs.question: Are global ERPs like SAP or Oracle compliant in Greece?
faqs.answer: Yes, but they usually require 'Localisation Packs' or middleware to handle specific Greek tax and payroll reporting.

faqs.question: Can I use software for paperless expense management?
faqs.answer: Yes, as long as the software creates MyDATA-compliant records, physical paper trails can be eliminated.

faqs.question: What is Ergani II ready?
faqs.answer: It refers to software that can communicate live with the second generation of the Greek labour platform, including QR work card functionality.

heroData.title: Marketing & Creative Services
heroData.subtitle: Grow Your Brand in the Greek & Global Markets
heroData.description: Leverage Athens' creative talent for your digital marketing, branding, and content strategies. We connect you with agencies that understand local consumer behavior and EU advertising standards.

steps.title: Market Research
steps.description: Analyzing the Greek competitive landscape and defining target personas (e.g. Gen Z in Athens vs. Tourist market).

steps.title: Creative Briefing
steps.description: Defining the visual identity and tone of voice, ensuring it resonates with local cultural nuances.

steps.title: Channel Strategy
steps.description: Selecting between Meta, TikTok, and local PR outlets based on the campaign objectives.

steps.title: Production & Execution
steps.description: Creating video content, localized copy, and setting up ad campaigns.

steps.title: Optimization
steps.description: Monitoring ROAS (Return on Ad Spend) and adjusting creatives based on real-time performance data.

items.title: Social Dominance
items.text: Greece has one of the highest social media engagement rates in Europe, particularly on Instagram and TikTok for consumer goods.

items.title: Language Nuance
items.text: Direct translations of English marketing copy often fail. 'Transcreation' by local Greek copywriters is mandatory for effective engagement.

items.title: Influencer Impact
items.text: Local influencers in the lifestyle, food, and tech niches have very high trust levels compared to traditional TV advertising.

items.title: SEE (Sumboulio Elenchou Epikoinonias)
items.text: Adhere to the Greek Code of Advertising-Communication Practice enforced by the SEE.

items.title: Influencer Disclosure
items.text: Paid partnerships must be clearly labeled (e.g., #adv or #ad) to comply with consumer protection laws.

items.title: GDPR for Marketing
items.text: Strict 'opt-in' rules for email marketing and SMS campaigns are enforced by the HDPA.

faqs.question: Can I run campaigns for all of Greece from Athens?
faqs.answer: Yes, most major agencies are based in Athens but handle nationwide and sometimes Balkan-wide campaigns.

faqs.question: Is Google Search or Social better in Greece?
faqs.answer: For lead gen, Google Search is dominant. For brand awareness and e-commerce, Meta and TikTok currently perform best.

faqs.question: What is the typical lead time?
faqs.answer: Major campaigns usually require 4-6 weeks for research and creative production.
